name: Agni-V intercontinental ballistic missile
overview_md:
The Agni-V is the apex of India's land-based nuclear deterrent — a long-range, solid-fuelled ballistic missile that, for the first time, lets India hold all of China at risk from launchers deep inside its own territory. Developed by DRDO and inducted from the early 2020s, it is the backbone of India's credible-minimum-deterrence posture against its principal strategic rival.

With a range generally cited at around 5,000–5,500 km (and assessed by some to be greater), the Agni-V brings every major Chinese city within reach. It is a three-stage, solid-fuel missile designed for canisterised, road- or rail-mobile launch, which keeps it concealed, survivable and ready to fire at short notice. In 2024, India tested a multiple independently-targetable re-entry vehicle (MIRV) capability under "Mission Divyastra," allowing a single missile to carry several warheads — a significant step in sophistication.

For an analyst, the Agni-V is the strategic counterweight in the India–China relationship. Where shorter-range Agni variants covered Pakistan, the Agni-V extends deterrence to Beijing and beyond, and the move to MIRVs and canisterised mobility mirrors the maturation of other Asian missile forces. It is a relatively small but symbolically and strategically weighty piece of the Indo-Pacific nuclear balance.

combat_history.event: India flight-tested an Agni-V with MIRV capability under 'Mission Divyastra'.
combat_history.significance: Demonstrated multiple-warhead capability — a major leap for India's deterrent.

combat_history.event: Successful test ahead of induction into the Strategic Forces Command.

modernization.description: MIRV deployment and reported longer-range Agni follow-ons.
modernization.impact: Increases warhead count and reach of India's deterrent.

vulnerabilities.description: A modest deterrent force under a declared no-first-use policy.
vulnerabilities.context: Survivability and second-strike are the priorities.

vulnerabilities.description: Must penetrate improving Chinese missile defences.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Concealed canisterised road/rail-mobile launchers for survivable second-strike.
key_operating_areas: targets: all of China and beyond

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's IRBM force is far larger and more mature; the Agni-V is India's primary China-spanning deterrent.
Both are emerging-power long-range missiles; the Agni-V is solid-fuelled and canisterised.
China's longer-range MIRVed ICBM dwarfs the Agni-V in reach and numbers.

doctrine.role: Long-range land-based nuclear ballistic missile providing India a China-spanning deterrent.
doctrine.employment: Concealed canisterised mobile launch for survivable second-strike under a no-first-use policy.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Credible minimum deterrence — reach all of China survivably, now with MIRVs.
doctrine.threat_context: The strategic counterweight in the India–China relationship.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's DF-26/DF-41 and North Korea's Hwasong-17.
